title: I/O-aware request coalescer + kernel orchestration to cut embedding endpoint tail latency
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Embedding endpoint p99s increase under mixed small and large request workloads. Current micro-batching strategy groups by arrival time only and sometimes dispatches suboptimal kernels for small batch shapes, causing I/O stalls and GPU kernel launch overheads. This ticket implements an I/O-aware coalescer that accounts for request-size distribution, NIC batching, and kernel warmup to reduce p99 without regressing throughput or cost.

Goals: Reduce p99 embedding latency by >= 30% for small-requests-heavy traces while keeping p50 within +/-10% and not increasing overall token cost by more than 5%. Provide safe rollout and observability to detect regressions.

Success metrics: p99 latency for embeddings on production-like small-request trace (emb-rls-2025-01) decreases >= 30%; p90 decreases >= 15%. No increase in 95th-percentile GPU utilization or token-cost by >5%. No customer-facing errors during canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler deployable behind runtime feature flag
p99 improvement >= 30% measured on emb-rls-2025-01 trace in loadtest and mirrored production traffic
Rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback on error/latency regressions
Dashboard panels (per-route p50/p90/p99, kernel selection heatmap, coalescer queue depth) added to Console
proposed_solution:
Design an I/O-aware coalescer that: (1) tags incoming requests with 'shape' metadata (batch size, vector-length, quantized flag), (2) maintains multiple small-window queues that opportunistically coalesce compatible small requests within 2ms windows, (3) applies a kernel-selection hint to the runtime so the scheduler can prefer low-launch-overhead kernels for tiny batches, and (4) uses a fast-path GPU warmup for known frequent shapes to amortize launch latency. The coalescer will interact with the existing adaptive microbatch scheduler but enforce an upper wait bound and prioritize NIC-level batch grouping (gRPC multiplexing) to reduce TCP syscall overheads.

Key implementation pieces: coalescer state machine (in request router), per-shape kernel hint table, kernel warmup pool (short-lived dummy invocation to populate caches), metrics hooks, and a feature-flag guarded rollout.

Rollout: unit tests -> internal perf loadtest -> blue/green canary on 1% of traffic -> gradual ramp to 25% with automated rollback thresholds -> full rollout.
experiment_results: Local perf test (gpu-a100-sim): baseline p99 420ms, with coalescer p99 280ms (33% reduction) on small-request trace (1-4 vectors). p90 improved from 210ms to 160ms.
End-to-end staging mirror: baseline p99 465ms, with coalescer 305ms (34% reduction). GPU utilization increased 3% but token/unit cost unchanged within noise +/-2%.
Kernel warmup reduced first-call overhead from 25ms to 6ms for frequent tiny shapes in microbenchmarks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coalescing increases single-request latency for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: allow per-customer opt-out and a strict max-wait (2ms) hard cap plus immediate bypass for flagged low-latency routes.
Risk: Wrong kernel hints could reduce throughput. Mitigation: conservative defaults, metrics-based selector, and quick rollback flag to revert to current kernel selection.
Risk: Increased memory pressure from kernel warmup pool. Mitigation: bounded warmup pool and LRU eviction of warmup slots.
Risk: Interactions with Dedicated capacity autoscaler. Mitigation: test on dedicated cluster and coordinate with infra team (dependency).
